The petitioner herein is an accused in Crime No.02/2023 of Koppal Women Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 344, 376(2)(n) of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") and Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (for short "POCSO") Act 2012, pending on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, at Koppal in Spl.SC.POCSO No.11/2023.
3.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case:
The mother of the victim has lodges a complaint stating that her daughter who is aged about 17 years and 2 months was studying in I year PUC in a Government Girls P.U College, Koppal, found missing.
It is further stated that, the said daughter/victim informed her mother NC: 2023:KHC-D:13404 who is a complainant herein on 31.12.2022 that she would go to college and return in the evening.
However, the victim had not returned to home till evening.
When it was enquired with their relatives and other friends regarding whereabouts of the victim, the complainant did not get any possible information.

Even though, after lapse of several days, the victim did not return to home, suspecting that the victim might have been abducted by some unknown person, the complainant decided to lodge a complaint against Shankarappa Hosalli who is the petitioner herein.
The jurisdictional police have conducted investigation.
During the investigation, they found that the petitioner abducted the victim on the pretext of marriage.
He was arrested on 12.01.2023 and produced him before the jurisdictional Magistrate.
4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that the victim girl was loving the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13404 petitioner, both the petitioner and the victim have decided to marry each other.
Accordingly, both have eloped to Hatti village situated near Kamanuru and stayed for a day.
It is stated that the petitioner had sexual intercourse on the said day.
Thereafter, on 11.01.2023 both petitioner and the victim had been to Koppal for Gavisiddeshwara fair and she was left alone in the said fair and the petitioner went away.
Thereafter, the police have secured her presence and took her to the police station.
Hence, the complaint.
The jurisdictional police have conducted investigation and submitted charge sheet.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that, the petitioner was not aware about the actual age of the victim.
Both victim and petitioner were loving each other and they have decided to marry each other.
The victim did not disclose her actual age when she was going along with the petitioner.
6. It is further submitted that, the petitioner is a tender aged boy, if he is in judicial custody there is likelihood of being influenced by the inmates of the jail.
The petitioner will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

7. Per contra Smt. Girija S. Hiremath, the learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition by filing objection and submitted that the offence committed against Women and Children are to be looked into very seriously in dealing with bail application.
The petitioner herein knowingly that the victim was a minor, induced her and abducted her and confined for a period of above 10 days and committed sexual intercourse on several occasions
. Thereby, the petitioner committed heinous offence.
Therefore, he is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, the submission of the learned counsel for the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13404 petitioner is that the age of the victim not known to the petitioner is nowhere concerned in the statement of the victim.
It is said that victim had disclosed the age before she was going with him.
9. It is further noticed that, as per the statement of the victim, she went along with the petitioner in a bus voluntarily and stayed with him without intimating the family members.
It is needless to say that the victim and the petitioner were loving each other and they were deciding to marry each other.
When the family members have objected, they decided to elope and went to different places and lastly she was found in Gavisiddeshwara fair.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances and also age of the victim, it is appropriate to grant bail by imposing suitable conditions.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.02/2023 of Koppal Women Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 344, 376(2)(n) of "IPC" and Section 6 of POCSO Act 2012, pending on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, at Koppal in Spl.SC.POCSO No.11/2023 on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:

b) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court till disposal of the case.
c) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.

In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above,
the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
